question: In which year was the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) policy was launched in India?
solution: The correct answer is __**2000**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Special Economic Zones (SEZs) policy** in India was introduced in the year **2000** to promote trade, investment, and economic growth. • SEZs are areas within a country that are subject to distinct economic regulations compared to other regions, aimed at increasing **industrial output**, **exports**, and **job creation**. • The **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** of India formulated the SEZ policy to provide an internationally competitive environment for businesses. • The SEZ policy was designed to attract **foreign direct investment (FDI)**, simplify procedures, and facilitate infrastructure development. • India's SEZs are governed under the **Special Economic Zones Act, 2005**, which provides the legal framework for their establishment and operation.
